Overstatement falls from 97% (base) to 35% (Nautil-SFT); the share of causal claims backed by evidence the model actually read rises from 26% to 78%; and answers that are both right about the cause and not overstated rise from 3% to 43%, against 9% for Gemini. The rate of naming the right cause barely moves (54% to 56%), and Gemini’s is higher (84%): the frontier model finds causes but states them beyond what the file supports. The contrast is sharpest on officially undetermined cases: Gemini closes 17 of these 41 cases, and the judge, given an undetermined reference, rates all 17 conclusions as overstated, while Nautil-SFT leaves 15 of the same 17 open. Nautil-SFT answers that make no causal claim at all are, without exception, case not closed answers. Overstatement rates depend on the judge (Sonnet 5: 11% for Nautil-SFT, 55% for Gemini), but the ranking holds, and all three judges find trained models overstate far less (Appendix C ). The limitation is on the other side of the decision: when Nautil-SFT leaves a case open, its gap is often generic (gap score 0.38 against Gemini’s 0.96), naming the specific missing evidence in 32% of unclosed answers. 6.4 Which components matter, and what does RL add? Without them, the model never leaves a case open (0.0%) and overstates in 84% of its answers (Table 5 ). Without the hypothesis ledger, closure depends less on the evidence. Removing it leaves accuracy slightly higher but within noise of Nautil-SFT (76.3 vs. 69.2), while the counterfactual effect shrinks from − - 26.1 to − - 8.7; the difference is clear on all 62 cases, and its interval reaches zero on the 23 non-host cases. Data scale matters: 10%, 50% and 100% of the trajectories give 45.9, 64.9 and 69.2 (the number of steps grows with the data). A closure-only reward gives the largest and cleanest RL gain. It raises balanced accuracy by 14.1 points and within-source accuracy from 60.4 to 74.1, removes missing closure markers (5.2% to 0), and shortens investigations (5.5 to 4.6 turns); the OOD gain (5.3 points) is within noise. Adding the judged checklist to the reward is harmful: counted on every rollout, it drives the policy towards never closing (17.4% of should-close cases closed at step 10); counted only when the decision is right, it avoids the collapse but gains only 3.8 points. A likely reason: when every rollout in a group is wrong, the checklist still ranks the wrong answers, and this spills over into reluctance to close. The closure-only reward has a measurable cost: the counterfactual effect shrinks ( − - 26.1 to − - 15.9; − - 23.3 to − - 5.0 without leaks), addressing alternatives drops (38% to 17%), and the conclusion score falls by 0.05: a trade-off between accuracy and evidence dependence, with Nautil-SFT and Nautil-RLVR at its two ends. 6.5 Further results Prompting and single-turn abstention training do not substitute. ReAct prompting (47.7) and our ledger format as a prompt (55.3, with 95% overstatement) leave the base model’s closing habit intact (Table 2 ). Abstain-R1 (27.9) and its base model (39.2) mostly fail to finish a multi-turn investigation (44% and 32% of runs end without a closure marker): abstention learned on single questions does not carry over to evidence gathering. Out of distribution and long files. OOD balanced accuracy rises from 50.6 (base) to 61.7 (Nautil-SFT) and 67.0 (Nautil-RLVR), close to Gemini (68.9). Because domain and label are tied in this set, this mostly reflects the direction of the decision; within individual domains no model is clearly above chance (Appendix D ). On the 20 largest files, Nautil-RLVR closes 93% of should-close cases when fetching its own evidence and 61% when given the whole file, which in turn matches the main cause more often (Appendix E ). Appendix Figure 7 shows a failure in which Nautil-SFT misreads a valve test. 7 Limitations Labels and sources. The source of a case still predicts its label, so accuracy is paired with within-source and counterfactual tests; the within-source metric rests mostly on board cases. Host labels are teacher judgments the teacher does not reproduce; host results are in the appendix. Judge, teacher and samples. GPT-6 Sol is both teacher and main judge, so its investigator row is only a reference; two further judges agree on direction but not on absolute rates. API models are mostly sampled once; the non-host counterfactual set has 23 cases, and its grounds are defined by the teacher’s citations. The Nautil-RLVR checkpoint was screened on 30 test cases, and a 33-case pilot set consulted while choosing the SFT epoch overlaps the OOD test set. Data. About 4% of references have extraction errors, some anonymised words are damaged, and trajectories retrace the report rather than explore. Open side of the decision. When our models leave a case open they often do not name the specific missing evidence, where frontier models are far ahead; and Nautil-RLVR depends less on the evidence than Nautil-SFT. 8 Conclusion Closing a case only when the evidence supports it is a judgment that does not come with capability: a frontier model finds causes more often than ours and an untrained model about as often, yet both close cases their reports leave undetermined and overstate what the evidence shows. Trained on audited investigation trajectories, a 9B model gains restraint and grounding: its closures move with the evidence, its claims cite what it read, and its conclusions are far less often overstated. A closure-only RL reward lifts accuracy to the teacher’s level at some cost in evidence dependence, whereas rewarding judged conclusion quality collapses the policy into never closing. Because a case’s source can stand in for its evidence, closure accuracy should be reported with a source-only baseline, within sources, and with evidence dependence.
